question: Firefighters in all EU Member States – especially in urban and industrial areas – are exposed daily to extremely high occupational risks, such as toxic fumes, carcinogens, asbestos, chemicals from burning materials and extreme temperatures in forest fires, with prolonged physical exhaustion.

The World Health Organization (WHO), through the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), which is the competent body for classifying carcinogens, has ranked the profession of firefighter in Group 1 ‘Carcinogenic to humans’, i.e. the highest category of carcinogens, on the basis of sufficient evidence that occupational exposure as a firefighter causes cancer in humans.

The EU Strategic Framework on Health and Safety at Work 2021-2027 and Directive 2004/37/EC set as key objectives the prevention of occupational diseases, the protection of workers from hazardous substances and the adoption of the ‘Vision Zero’ approach to workrelated deaths. On the basis of the above: 1.
Will the Commission provide financial support to national, local and regional authorities for the modernisation of personal protective equipment and the decontamination of equipment and uniforms?
Will the Commission provide funding in the 2028-2034 MFF for the implementation of the upcoming updated Directive 2004/37/EC?
Will the Commission include firefighters and rescue workers in the new EU Strategic Framework on Health and Safety at Work 2028-2034?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2026) The Commission supports, through EU funding instruments, preparedness, prevention and response capacities in Member States. It has also supported financially the stockpiling of critical equipment, including personal protective equipment, and measures to strengthen the resilience of health and civil protection systems in emergencies.

The co-legislators reached a provisional agreement on 23 June 2026 on the sixth revision of the Carcinogens, Mutagens and Reprotoxic Substances Directive (CMRD1). The next Multiannual Financial Framework and the National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs), encourage Member States to invest in line with European priorities, according to their national, regional and local needs.

Measures to support the implementation of an updated CMRD could be part of this if the measures contribute to the objectives of the regulation. The current EU occupational safety and health (OSH) strategic framework2 aims to protect all workers and runs until 2027. The content of a possible strategic framework after 2027 will involve consultations with relevant stakeholders.

The Communication on integrated wildfire risk management3, adopted in March 2026, and the Council Recommendation on integrated wildfire risk management4, adopted in June 2026 highlight that firefighters need adequate protection, equipment, training, and assets, in line with OSH standards, underlining that they are exposed to various health risks.

These can be mitigated through adequate training, appropriate protective equipment, and accessible health support, among others. By 2028, the Commission intends to launch a study to promote monitoring of firefighters’ exposure to wildfires and possible related long-term health impacts.
